title: Preservation across setting a memory bit
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,\ldots,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Suppose the machine instruction at state $l$ sets the memory bit at the head to true and continues at $l'$. Let $st$ be a register state with every one of its 17 counters at most $B$, let $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be the memory contents, and suppose the head position $p$ satisfies $0\le p\le P$. If the machine can reach a configuration $c$ from state $l'$ with state $st$, memory updated to true at $p$, and head at $p$, with every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfying the guard, then it can reach the same $c$ from state $l$ with state $st$, original memory $M$, and head at $p$, again satisfying the guard at every configuration strictly before the endpoint. The guard requires that all register values are at most $B$, the head position lies in $[0,P]$, and the current instruction meets its operand conditions.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle on four indices and Boolean words
Instruction at $l$ is a memory-set instruction continuing at $l'$
All 17 counters of $st$ are at most $B$
Reachability from the post-instruction configuration while maintaining the guard before the endpoint
replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let
$\mathrm{orc}:\mathrm{Fin}(4)\to\mathrm{List}(\mathrm{Bool})\to\mathrm{Bool}$ be an
oracle, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Suppose a machine instruction at control state
$l$ sets the memory bit at the head to true and continues at $l'$. Let $st$ be a
register state whose 17 counters are all at most $B$, let the head position $p$ satisfy
$0\le p\le P$, and suppose $c$ is reachable from the configuration at $l'$ with the
memory updated to true at $p$ and the head at $p$, while maintaining the guard at every
earlier step. Then $c$ is reachable from the configuration at $l$ with the original
memory and head position $p$, while maintaining that guard at every earlier step.
